subject: Alzheimer's Shrinks the Amygdala and Entorhinal Cortex Years Before Memory Loss
script: From Agewell Brief: Alzheimer's Shrinks the Amygdala and Entorhinal Cortex Years Before Memory Loss. Volume loss in two gateway structures tracks the early spatial spread of misfolded tau tangles long before hippocampal damage occurs. Before Alzheimer's disease disrupts memory, it silently dismantles brain architecture over a five- to ten-year window. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
